prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an L-shaped kitchen and background dining area as the camera wearer turns left and walks past another person from the stove area toward the sink across the 5 frames. In frames 1 and 2, a white upper cabinet on the right is extremely close (0.3–0.5 m, within the wearer's arm's reach) and a man standing on the left (roughly 1.2 m away in frame 1 and 0.6–0.8 m in frame 2) faces right and downward toward a frying pan on the stove within his arm's reach, never looking at the camera wearer. In frame 3, the camera wearer passes closely to the left of the man, whose back/shoulder is partially visible at the far right edge (~0.4 m away), while the sink counter sits 1.5–2 m ahead and a dining table with chairs lies 3–4 m behind it on the left. Across frames 4 and 5, the wearer approaches the counter and bends forward until the dual sink basins, faucet, and dish soap bottle are directly in front and below at 0.4–0.8 m (well within arm's reach), with upper cabinets overhanging above. This map clarifies the continuous distance gradient from the foreground cabinets and person to the background room and highlights the protruding 3D silhouettes of the microwave, yellow-lidded jar, and soap bottle against the counter and tile backsplash, though it becomes blurry and unreliable around the open dishwasher rack in frame 3 and in frame 5 where motion blur flattens the counter items and sink basins.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels discrete objects across the scene as the camera wearer turns left past the man at the stove (frames 1–3) and approaches the sink counter (frames 4–5). It identifies the man on the left in frame 1 (~1.2 m away, partly out of view at the left edge), near the center-left in frame 2 (~0.7 m away, facing right toward the stove), and partially occluded at the right edge of frame 3 (~0.4 m away) as the wearer moves past him. Surrounding kitchen and dining objects are segmented at varying distances, including bowls and cups on the far counter ~1.5–2 m behind the man in frames 1–2, dining chairs ~3–4 m away on the left in frames 2–3, the open dishwasher ('oven'), microwave, and sink counter ~1.5–2 m ahead in frame 3, and a soap bottle and sink basin ~0.8–1 m ahead and within arm's reach in frame 4. While the map helps isolate small distant tableware and background chairs that blend into the cluttered RGB background, it is highly unreliable across the strip: it misclassifies the black frying pan held in the man's right hand in frame 2 as a 'person', labels the open dishwasher below the counter as an 'oven' in frame 3, misidentifies the right-hand sink basin as a 'laptop' in frame 4, and detects nothing at all in the close-up frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks only sparse upper-body and facial keypoints (yellow) for the man standing at the stove in frames 1 and 2, while frames 3 through 5 are completely empty as he falls behind the camera wearer's field of view. In frame 1, facial keypoints on the far left (~1.2 m away, with his torso cropped out of the left frame edge) show his head in right profile, facing and looking downward to the right toward the counter rather than at the camera wearer. In frame 2, as the camera wearer moves closer (~0.7 m away) and turns left, the cluster of head keypoints and a single shoulder-to-neck segment confirm he remains oriented to the right and tilted downward toward the stove within his arm's reach. These head landmarks provide a clean geometric readout of his profile gaze direction without needing to resolve his dark glasses and hair in the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable because it misses nearly his entire torso and arms in frames 1 and 2, fails to detect any magenta hand skeletons even when his right hand holds the pan handle in frame 2, and misses his partially visible torso at the right edge of frame 3.
